subject: Discovery: multilingual model fit & evals (Globex Retail)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@globexretail.de>; John Miller <john.miller@globexretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: multilingual model fit & evals (Globex Retail)

Hi Anna / John —

Great to meet you earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

Summary of needs:
- Multilingual NLU for storefront search suggestions and help center routing across DE/FR/ES (EU) and ZH/JA/KO (APAC).
- Strong locale-specific quality, particularly German/French business terminology and Chinese product names.
- Soft latency target: 200–400ms p95 for single-turn suggestions; throughput for batch reprocessing ~50 req/s.
- Data residency: prefer EU region for EU traffic.

Recommended model candidates for evaluation (shortlist):
1) redwood-rlhf-7b-q4f — good latency/cost balance, strong English + decent EU language transfer (fast inference).
2) redwood-quant-13b-multi — higher quality for FR/DE/ES, slightly higher cost; recommend for critical UX paths.
3) open-mx-30b-eu-tuned — best raw quality on FR/DE but needs validation on product names and brand tokens.

Deliverables we can provide this week:
- Evaluation spreadsheet with benchmark slices per locale (attached: globex_evals_v1.xlsx).
- Prompt sets covering common intents + locale examples (attached: prompt_set_fr_de_es.txt).
- Latency and cost breakdown by model (attached: latency_cost_breakdown.pdf).
- Short test harness / eval dashboard link: https://redwood.ai/evals/GLX-2027

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a small representative test set (~500 queries across locales) or allow us to run synthetic probes on anonymized example inputs.
2) We run per-model evals (quality metrics + latency/cost) and return a prioritized recommendation and configuration (batching, quantization) within 3 business days.
3) Schedule a follow-up to review results and decide on a pilot (can be EU-only first).

Can you confirm you can share a small test set this week, or should we generate synthetic probes for an initial pass?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
https://redwood.ai

----
Attachments: globex_evals_v1.xlsx; prompt_set_fr_de_es.txt; latency_cost_breakdown.pdf

From: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@globexretail.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Miller <john.miller@globexretail.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Discovery: multilingual model fit & evals (Globex Retail)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments — very helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) For German and French specifically, do you have examples from the eval spreadsheet that show failure modes (false positives for brand names, issues with declension/formality)?
2) Can you call out expected cost delta between the 7b quant vs the 13b quant candidate for production traffic at our estimated volume (~100k suggestions/day)?
3) For EU data residency, do you run inference in eu-west-1 by default for EU traffic? We have compliance constraints about logs and KV cache retention.

We can share a labeled sample of ~400 queries across DE/FR/ES by EOD Wednesday. Would that be sufficient? Also looping in Li Wei on APAC localization questions — Li, would you be able to provide ~100 Chinese queries (product titles + colloquial search)?

Best,
Anna Schmidt
Head of Search & Personalization | Globex Retail
anna.schmidt@globexretail.de | +49 30 5555 1234

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: multilingual model fit & evals (Globex Retail)

Marissa / Anna —

Quick technical notes from infra/qa perspective based on the requested slices: 

- EU residency: We can pin inference to eu-west-1 and ensure logs/audit events are stored in a customer-controlled KMS-backed bucket. We will populate a configuration snippet in the follow-up report.
- Latency: redwood-rlhf-7b-q4f typically hits ~120–220ms p95 under 4x batching on the Dedicated profile; redwood-quant-13b-multi is ~200–380ms p95 depending on sequence length. We'll include latency-by-sequence-length in the report.
- Quality regression concerns: Our eval harness will run the new models against your historical golden set plus differential tests for brand tokens. If we see regressions >3% on top-k intent accuracy for a locale, we'll flag and propose prompt/temperature adjustments or a heavier-weight model for that slice.
- APAC languages: For CJK (ZH/JA/KO), tokenization differences matter — we'll recommend a byte-level tokenizer-friendly quant profile and run targeted prompt patterns for product name preservation.

I can take lead on running the automated evals once we have the test samples.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
SRE / Inference QA, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Hi Anna —

Thanks — that sounds perfect. A few answers and clarifications inline: 

1) Sample size: 400 DE/FR/ES + 100 ZH will be great for an initial pass. Please include any failing examples you already know of (examples with brand-name collisions or formal/informal variants).
2) Cost delta: At your estimated volume (~100k suggestions/day), rough monthly tokenized inference cost estimate (production, not including infra reserved capacity):
   - redwood-rlhf-7b-q4f: ~$1,800–2,200/month (with aggressive batching and prefix caching)
   - redwood-quant-13b-multi: ~$3,400–4,200/month (higher tokens/sec cost but better locale quality)
   We'll include a token-level breakdown in the latency_cost_breakdown.pdf and in the follow-up.
3) Residency: Neha confirmed we can pin to eu-west-1 and keep logs under your KMS. We will also provide the SOC2 artifact pointers if you need them.

Next steps I will own:
- Run evaluations vs your sample once received; produce per-locale metrics table and concrete prompt recommendations.
- If we see regression risks on DE/FR, propose a hybrid approach: 13b for critical DE/FR intents + 7b for fallthroughs to reduce cost.

Can you drop the files to the Drive folder I shared (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C) or reply with the CSVs? I'll confirm ETA for the eval by end of day Friday.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
